engine_name: vLLM (vllm-project), v0.19.0+ (Gemma 4 support landed in v0.19.0, released April 2026 in a 14-day window alongside v0.18.0/v0.19.1rc0; default PyPI CUDA moved to 13.0 in v0.20.0). High-throughput inference engine with PagedAttention, continuous batching, and an OpenAI-compatible server. This research item assumed a source build is mandatory on CUDA 12.8 — that premise is LARGELY FALSE (see cuda_128_compatible): vLLM publishes cu128 pre-built wheels, so a source build is usually NOT required.
cuda_128_compatible: Yes — and the task premise ('ALL pre-built wheels require CUDA 12.9+') is INCORRECT. vLLM officially publishes binaries compiled against CUDA 12.8, 12.9, and 13.0. The vLLM GPU install docs explicitly support a cu128 path: `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128`, or with uv `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=cu128`. There are also per-release GitHub wheel assets following the pattern `vllm-${VER}+cu128-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl`. Driver 570.x fully supports the CUDA 12.8 runtime, and the A6000 is sm_86 (Ampere GA102), a first-class, long-supported vLLM target — so the cu128 wheel runs out of the box on this host. CAVEATS: (1) the DEFAULT PyPI wheel moved to cu130 in v0.20.0 and the headline install assumes cu129, so you MUST pass the cu128 extra-index/torch-backend explicitly or pip will pull a cu129/cu130 torch that mismatches the 12.8 driver; (2) one documented gap — Issue #37847 reports the v0.18.0 cu128 GitHub release wheel URL 404'd, so verify the specific version's cu128 asset exists before pinning a direct URL (the PyPI `--extra-index-url cu128` path is more reliable than hand-built GitHub URLs). Source build is therefore a FALLBACK, not a requirement. IF you do build from source for sm_86: clone, install cu128 torch, `export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='8.6'`, `pip install -r requirements/build.txt`, `pip install --no-build-isolation -e .` — a heavy (tens of minutes to hours), brittle compile that is unnecessary given the working cu128 wheel. [uncertain] exact lowest vLLM version with a published cu128 wheel asset.
gemma4_support: Yes — full first-class support. Google Gemma 4 architecture (Gemma4ForCausalLM) landed in vLLM v0.19.0 via PR #38826 (lucianommartins, merged by ywang96, commit 08ed2b9) plus follow-ups #39027 and bugfix #38847, requiring transformers>=5.5.0. Covers all variants: E2B, E4B, 26B-A4B (MoE), and 31B (dense), including multimodal vision/video, dual local+global attention, native reasoning trace parsing, and structured tool use. google/gemma-4-31B-it is explicitly listed in the vLLM Recipes Gemma 4 guide. Required format: HuggingFace safetensors (NOT GGUF/EXL2). Quant options available on HF and supported by vLLM: (a) Google's official QAT W4A16 checkpoint `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct` (compressed-tensors, group_size=32, 4-bit int weights / 16-bit activations) — vLLM auto-detects the quant config, no flag needed, best 4-bit quality; (b) NVIDIA's `nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4` (FP4, served with `--quantization modelopt`); (c) bitsandbytes online int4 via `--quantization bitsandbytes --load-format bitsandbytes` (works single-GPU; tensor-parallel bnb has known hangs). Architectural gaps are bug-level, not missing-feature (see known_issues_gemma4).
per_request_reasoning_toggle: Yes — works per-request and is documented. Server launched with `--reasoning-parser gemma4`. Two equivalent per-request mechanisms on /v1/chat/completions: (1) the OpenAI-standard `reasoning_effort` field — vLLM maps 'low'/'medium'/'high' -> enable_thinking=true and 'none' -> enable_thinking=false, auto-injecting into chat_template_kwargs; (2) explicit `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true/false}}`, which takes priority over reasoning_effort if both set. Gemma 4 reasoning is OFF by default; you must opt in. Server-wide default available via `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`. KNOWN FOOTGUN (Issue #39130): with `enable_thinking: false` the prompt contains no <|channel> tokens, so the gemma4 reasoning parser's is_reasoning_end() returns False and SILENTLY DISABLES structured output (xgrammar) — i.e. guided-decoding/JSON-schema requests can be bypassed when thinking is off. Mitigation discussed in issues: set `"skip_special_tokens": false` to preserve delimiters so the parser maps reasoning to message.reasoning correctly. So the toggle works but interacts badly with structured output when off.
per_request_reasoning_budget: Yes — this is vLLM's key advantage over llama.cpp here, and it solves the exact problem in the task. PR #37112 ('[Feature] Add reasoning_budget to cap thinking tokens via existing reasoning parser', by abhinand5) is MERGED into main and caps thinking tokens per request via the existing reasoning parser. Per-request fields: `reasoning_budget` (integer, e.g. 50 or 512) caps thinking at ~N tokens, after which an injection message forces the model to stop thinking and answer; a custom `reasoning_budget_message` (e.g. 'Stop thinking and answer now.') is supported. The request-level argument is also referred to as `thinking_token_budget`. It works through the gemma4 reasoning parser (vllm/reasoning/gemma4_reasoning_parser.py registered in vllm/reasoning/__init__.py), so it applies to Gemma 4. vLLM release notes also state speculative decoding now respects reasoning/thinking budgets. Practical guidance from community testing: 500-1000 token budgets retain most accuracy vs unbounded thinking. CAVEAT: vLLM's official docs list only a few models under thinking_token_budget; Gemma 4 support is confirmed through the parser registration but is comparatively new — validate the exact field name (`reasoning_budget` vs `thinking_token_budget`) against your installed version. [uncertain] whether the budget injection is 100% reliable for Gemma 4 specifically across all 0.19.x patch versions.
tool_calling_support: Dedicated parser. Launch with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja`. Gemma 4 emits a CUSTOM (non-JSON) serialization: `<|tool_call>call:func_name{key:<|"|>value<|"|>,num:42}<tool_call|>` with bare unquoted keys, <|"|> (token 52) string delimiter, and concatenated multi-calls. The Gemma4ToolParser uses an accumulate-then-parse-then-diff streaming strategy rather than token-by-token JSON conversion. KNOWN FAILURE MODES (important for an agent at 4-8 parallel sub-agents): (1) Issue #39392 — under CONCURRENT requests the gemma4 tool parser produces outputs filled with <pad> tokens; the parser has shared mutable state that is not thread-safe, so request state leaks between concurrent calls (succeeds 100% sequentially, fails concurrently). This is a direct risk for the parallel-sub-agent workload. (2) Issue #39468 — vllm 0.19.0 returns incorrectly-formatted tool calls in some cases. (3) Issue #39043 — Gemma 4 + Claude Code tool-calling problems. (4) Bugfix #38847 was required so __init__ accepts the `tools` param (else 400 error). Verify your patch version includes the concurrency fix before relying on parallel tool calls.
openai_api_compatible: Yes — vLLM's whole serving model is the OpenAI-compatible server (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions) with SSE streaming, a near drop-in for openai-python / httpx asyncio clients. Serve on port 8000 with `--port 8000`. Deviations to handle in an asyncio client: (1) reasoning is returned in a separate `message.reasoning` / `reasoning_content` field (not `content`) when thinking is on; (2) the structured-output bypass when enable_thinking=false (Issue #39130) can silently ignore guided-decoding requests; (3) Gemma 4-specific extras (reasoning_effort/reasoning_budget/enable_thinking via chat_template_kwargs) ride in extra_body. Otherwise tool_calls, deltas, and streaming shape are standard OpenAI.
continuous_batching: Yes — a core strength and the spec's stated reason for preferring vLLM. vLLM does continuous batching with PagedAttention (paged KV cache) and prefix caching. For up to ~10 concurrent users and 4-8 parallel sub-agents this is comfortably within range and is genuine value over a sequential/llama.cpp baseline — multiple in-flight requests are interleaved at the token level rather than serialized. NOTE: the gemma4 tool-parser concurrency bug (#39392) is the one caveat that undercuts the concurrency story specifically for concurrent TOOL-CALLING requests until patched.
installation_steps:
Host-native on CUDA 12.8, no Docker, Ubuntu/Debian RunPod pod. PREFERRED PATH (pre-built cu128 wheel, NO source build):

# 1. Python 3.11 venv
python3.11 -m venv ~/.vllm && source ~/.vllm/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip

# 2A. Easiest: uv auto-selects/pins cu128
pip install uv
UV_TORCH_BACKEND=cu128 uv pip install 'vllm>=0.19.0'

# 2B. Or plain pip with the cu128 torch index (must pass it explicitly or you get cu129/cu130)
pip install 'vllm>=0.19.0' --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

# 3. Gemma 4 needs transformers>=5.5.0
pip install 'transformers>=5.5.0'

# 4. Verify
python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.get_device_capability())"  # expect 12.8 and (8, 6)

FALLBACK ONLY IF the cu128 wheel for your version is missing (e.g. #37847): build from source for sm_86
  git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git && cd vllm && git checkout v0.19.0
  pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
  export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='8.6' MAX_JOBS=$(nproc)
  pip install -r requirements/build.txt
  pip install --no-build-isolation -e .
  # Optional speedup if no kernel changes: VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 (reuses prebuilt kernels). Expect tens of minutes to hours; brittle on torch/CUDA version drift.

Build from source is NOT recommended here given the working wheel.
serve_command:
Recommended: Google's official QAT W4A16 checkpoint on a single A6000 (best 4-bit quality, auto-detected quant, leaves headroom for co-resident embedder/reranker), parsers + per-request reasoning control + tools enabled:

vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
  --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
  --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja

Notes: no --quantization flag needed for the qat-w4a16 checkpoint (vLLM reads it from the config). Per request, control reasoning with reasoning_effort ('none'/'low'/'medium'/'high') or chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking, and cap thinking with reasoning_budget. For bitsandbytes int4 of the base bf16 checkpoint instead, use `vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it --quantization bitsandbytes --load-format bitsandbytes` (single-GPU only). Cap --max-model-len at 16k to keep the KV cache small and preserve VRAM for the reranker; full 256K window would blow the budget. AVOID combining tool calling with speculative decoding (see speculative_decoding / Issue #41967). [uncertain] exact gpu-memory-utilization that leaves clean room for bge-reranker co-residency.
speculative_decoding: Yes — vLLM supports MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding for Gemma 4, added in PR #41745 (lucianommartins). For the 31B dense model, use Google's matching assistant checkpoint with method 'mtp' (NOT generic draft_model): `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","model":"google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`. The assistant checkpoints (E2B/E4B/12B/26B-A4B/31B) share the KV cache with the target for low overhead; if startup logs show method='draft_model' for an assistant checkpoint, your vLLM is too old — upgrade. N-gram speculative decoding (no draft model) is also available. IMPORTANT re the task's `mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf`: that is a GGUF/llama.cpp artifact and is NOT usable by vLLM — vLLM consumes the HF-format `*-assistant` safetensors checkpoint, not GGUF. CRITICAL BUG: Issue #41967 — Gemma 4 + MTP speculative decoding DROPS the first tool-call's argument deltas in streaming multi-tool auto-tool-choice. So do NOT enable MTP together with tool calling. Benchmarks (single H100) found MTP the better starting point for 31B dense vs DFlash, but real speedup is workload/hardware dependent and must be measured on the A6000. [uncertain] measured A6000-48GB single-stream speedup figure.
known_issues_gemma4: (1) Tool-parser concurrency bug — Issue #39392: gemma4 --tool-call-parser produces all-<pad> output under concurrent requests due to non-thread-safe shared parser state (succeeds sequentially); directly threatens the 4-8 parallel-sub-agent workload until patched. (2) Structured-output bypass — Issue #39130: --reasoning-parser gemma4 silently disables xgrammar/guided decoding when enable_thinking=false (is_reasoning_end returns False because no <|channel> tokens present); mitigate with skip_special_tokens=false. (3) reasoning_content not populated — Issue #38855: special tokens stripped (skip_special_tokens=True) before the parser sees them, so thinking leaks into content; parser lacked start_token_id/end_token_id (unlike Qwen3ReasoningParser). (4) Tool-call format wrong — Issue #39468 (vllm 0.19.0). (5) Claude Code tool-calling problems — Issue #39043. (6) Tool parser __init__ missing `tools` -> 400 error, fixed in #38847. (7) MTP spec-decode drops first tool-call args in streaming — Issue #41967. (8) Install: documented v0.18.0 cu128 wheel URL 404 — Issue #37847. Net: core architecture is solid in v0.19.0; the rough edges cluster around concurrency + tool-calling + reasoning-parser interactions, so pin a late 0.19.x patch and verify these fixes.
vram_usage: On the 48GB A6000 at 16k context, single stream: bf16 31B weights are ~62GB and do NOT fit a single A6000 (reported ~43.8GB for the bf16 model in one DEV.to test that appears to use a smaller/compressed load; the 62GB figure is full bf16 weights+overhead — treat bf16-on-one-A6000 as not safely fitting for 31B). 4-bit paths fit comfortably: QAT W4A16 / NVFP4 31B weights ~18-20GB, leaving ~25GB+ for KV cache at 16k plus headroom — the recommended single-A6000 option. bitsandbytes int4 of the 31B reportedly sits ~38GB used on a 48GB card for ~32B-class models (less efficient than W4A16). Co-resident BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (~0.13GB) + bge-reranker-v2-m3 (~2.3GB) ~2.4GB total fits alongside a W4A16/NVFP4 deployment comfortably; with bitsandbytes it is tight, lower --gpu-memory-utilization to ~0.75. [uncertain] exact KV-cache size at 16k for the 31B head config and precise co-residency margin.
small_scale_fit: Viable. The cu128 wheel removes the main feared obstacle (no mandatory source build), so operational overhead is moderate: a pip/uv install with an explicit cu128 backend, plus version pinning to a 0.19.x patch that has the Gemma 4 fixes. For 1 dev + up to 10 concurrent users and 4-8 sub-agents, PagedAttention + continuous batching give real headroom over a llama.cpp baseline, AND vLLM uniquely offers per-request reasoning_budget (the core capability llama.cpp lacks) plus a dedicated gemma4 tool parser. Single-A6000 forces a 4-bit checkpoint (W4A16/NVFP4), which is fine. Migrating later to a personal A6000 is seamless (same sm_86 target). The honest cost: a cluster of Gemma 4 tool-calling/concurrency/reasoning-parser bugs (esp. #39392) that you must verify are patched, and the cu128-vs-default-cu129/130 install gotcha. Heavier than llama.cpp but justified by reasoning_budget + tool parser + batching.
overall_recommendation: RECOMMENDED (with the major caveat that the task's framing is wrong). The premise 'ALL pre-built wheels require CUDA 12.9+, so a source build is needed' is incorrect: vLLM publishes cu128 wheels, so you should install the pre-built cu128 wheel and NOT build from source. A source build is a brittle, hours-long fallback only for the rare missing-wheel case (#37847). vLLM is the only engine in this comparison that delivers BOTH per-request reasoning_budget (PR #37112, solving the exact llama.cpp limitation) AND a dedicated gemma4 tool parser AND a gemma4 reasoning parser AND continuous batching/PagedAttention AND MTP speculative decoding — all on a fully-supported sm_86/CUDA-12.8 target. Pros: cu128 wheel works out of the box on driver 570.195; per-request enable_thinking + reasoning_budget; standard OpenAI API; best-in-class batching for parallel sub-agents; QAT W4A16 / NVFP4 4-bit checkpoints fit a single 48GB A6000 with room for the reranker. Cons: (1) must explicitly select cu128 (default wheel is cu129/cu130) or you get a driver mismatch; (2) a real cluster of Gemma 4 bugs to navigate — concurrency tool-parser <pad> bug (#39392), structured-output bypass (#39130), reasoning_content leakage (#38855), MTP+tool-call streaming (#41967) — so pin a late 0.19.x patch and verify fixes; (3) do not combine tool calling with MTP speculative decoding. Action: `UV_TORCH_BACKEND=cu128 uv pip install 'vllm>=0.19.x'` (latest patch), serve google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct with gemma4 parsers, 16k context, reasoning_budget per request, speculative decoding OFF when tools are in use. vs SGLang: vLLM is smoother on cu128 and has the reasoning_budget that SGLang lacks. vs ExLlamaV2: vLLM has the parsers, batching, and budget ExLlamaV2 lacks for this agentic workload.
